intro.uz: Fermer ota universitetda oʻqiyotgan oʻgʻliga issiq yoz va suv tanqisligi haqida xat yozadi. Oʻqishdan oldin oʻylab koʻring: havo isib borsa, dehqonlar nimalarni oʻzgartirishi kerak?

paragraphs.en: Dear Farrukh, thank you for your message and the photos from your university. Your mother says you have been studying hard, and we are both very proud of you. You asked me how the farm is doing this year, so I will tell you honestly: it has been the most difficult summer I can remember.

When I was your age, the hottest days of July felt like an exception. Now we seem to have weeks of extreme heat almost every summer, and the heat starts earlier in the year. The canal that waters our fields also carried less water this year than it used to. By August, the water was arriving only every few days, and the melons on the lower field had dried up before they were ready.

But I don't want you to think we are giving up. Your uncle and I have decided to change the way we farm. We have planted part of the land with sorghum, which needs less water than many other crops and can survive long dry periods. After the wheat harvest, we sowed mung beans, which grow quickly and are good for the soil. We have also started covering the soil between the plants with straw. It keeps the ground cooler and stops the water from evaporating so fast.

We are also working at different times. In June and July, we start in the fields before sunrise and rest in the hottest hours of the afternoon. Karim aka from the next village laughed at us at first, but last week he came and asked us how the straw method works. Next spring, I would like to plant a few rows of pistachio trees. They can handle heat and dry soil well, although they take several years to produce a harvest.

This is where you come in, my son. You are learning things at university that I never had the chance to learn. When you come home for the winter holidays, I want you to look at our fields and tell me what else we could do. If my grandfather saw how we farm today, he would not believe his eyes, but I think he would understand that we must change with the weather. Take care of yourself. Your father
